extracted.intended_audience: FCC program participants, service providers, marketing organizations, consultants, program administrators, and compliance officers involved with Lifeline, USF (E-Rate, RHC), TRS, and NDBEDP programs
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and program-specific supplemental standards governing who is a 'principal', disclosure obligations by primary and lower tier participants, timing and scope of disclosures, verification and retention requirements, and remedies for unfavorable disclosures across FCC universal service and related programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental definition — Lifeline/ACP marketing organization
rubrics_metrics.description: "Lifeline marketing organization" or "ACP marketing organization" as an entity that: (i) has a contractual relationship with the entity providing the Lifeline or ACP services to consumers for the purpose of securing Lifeline or ACP enrollments; or (ii) has any contract to provide for such Lifeline or ACP enrollment services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a program-specific supplemental definitional rule to identify entities that facilitate enrollments and therefore may be treated as principals under the supplemental definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per se principal rule for consultants and marketing organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants who have or had a business relationship with the participant in connection with a covered transaction and Lifeline or ACP marketing organizations shall be considered a principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopts a per se rule (no individualized fact-finding needed) because these professionals have often driven waste, fraud, and abuse; intended to provide clarity and administrability. Participants are urged to err on the side of disclosure in close cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second prong — critical influence or substantive control
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the "critical influence on or substantive control over" component to ensure certain forms of misconduct may be addressed even if not captured by the Guidelines' more narrow definition of principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prong permits exclusion or other remedies where a person's actions had a significant adverse effect on a transaction (e.g., causing ineligible registrations) even if they would not otherwise be a principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment representatives classified as lower tier participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrollment representatives of marketing organizations will be classified as lower tier participants and will not be deemed "principals" except in extraordinary circumstances as determined case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'enrollment representatives' has the same meaning as in the implicated Commission programs; their disclosure obligations are limited to those under section 180.355 of the Guidelines. Enrollment representatives should only disclose exclusion status to their marketing organization employer, and the marketing organization must retain these disclosures for the employment period or applicable document retention period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultant advice can ground exclusion if it causes misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidence demonstrates that a consultant's 'act of giving advice' was the cause of rule violations or misconduct by a program participant, then an exclusion might be appropriate depending on aggravating and mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultants may argue their advice was merely negligent (which weighs against exclusion) or that they did not cause the misconduct (which, if true, would preclude exclusion). The Commission evaluates causation and aggravating/mitigating circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary tier disclosure required items
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary tier participants must advise the agency if they are presently excluded or disqualified, and must state: (a) whether the participant or any principals have been convicted within the preceding three years of any offenses listed in §180.800(a) or had a civil judgment rendered against them for one of those offenses within that time period; (b) are presently indicted for or otherwise criminally or civilly charged with any of those offenses; or (c) have had one or more public transactions terminated within the preceding three years for cause or default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the adopted Guidelines' disclosure requirements; disclosures should be made to the Commission and relevant program administrators. Most disclosures are not dispositive; agencies may consider additional information when deciding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification — funding denial is not a 'termination' per se
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere denial of a funding request does not, without more, constitute a 'termination . . . for cause or default' of a public transaction as used by the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only termination of a previously approved funding request based on serious errors or misconduct (e.g., competitive bidding violations) is reportable as a termination. Parties may provide additional contextual information with disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report terminations even if pending appeal; do not report reversed/vacated terminations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not establish an exception for otherwise reportable terminations pending appeal; however, do not require reporting of terminations that have been reversed or vacated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of a pending termination does not automatically trigger denial; Commission can consider disclosed info and additional submissions and may allow transactions with heightened safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination reporting includes state and local transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary tier participants must report terminations of transactions with state and local governments (not limited to Federal transactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting stretches back three years; although potentially burdensome, such information is valuable when a participant lacks Federal history and helps assess fitness to participate in Commission programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures must be made to Commission and relevant program administrators (and beneficiaries in certain programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Such disclosures must be made not only to the Commission, but to the relevant program administrators; for certain programs service providers must also disclose to beneficiaries (e.g., E-Rate schools/libraries or RHC beneficiaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For E-Rate and RHC, disclosures should be made preferably early in the bid selection process and prior to provider selection and form submissions; WCB/CGB to modify program forms accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification to section 180.300 — verifications among same-tier participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify section 180.300 to require that the verifications required by that rule will be applicable not only to transactions with 'another person at the next lower tier' but to transactions among participants at the same tier as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because service providers and beneficiaries in E-Rate and RHC will be considered primary tier participants, verifications are necessary among same-tier participants to facilitate program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of primary-tier disclosures to lower tier participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend the Guidelines' primary tier disclosure requirements to lower tier participants in all Commission programs subject to this Report and Order; lower tier participants must make the broader disclosures to the Commission, program administrators, and the higher tier participant with which they seek to conduct business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This responds to lower tier participants (e.g., consultants, marketing organizations) being significant drivers of malfeasance. The rule is implemented with modifications and exceptions (e.g., enrollment representatives). Supplemental Rule 6001.330 governs related transaction clauses/conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures among lower tier participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Require disclosures among and between lower tier participants that enter into covered transactions with each other; the lower tier participant performing work must provide disclosures to any participant paying for the work or hiring them under the covered transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: E-Rate subcontractor must provide disclosures to the contractor before consummating the transaction; marketing organizations must provide disclosures to each other when performing work on behalf of another marketing entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection methods — SAM.gov insufficient for expanded info
rubrics_metrics.description: Checking SAM.gov Exclusions is appropriate for confirming exclusion/disqualification status but does not allow a primary tier participant to verify the additional information required from lower tier participants under the supplemental rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional disclosures should be obtained through collecting certifications or including clauses/conditions in covered transactions; consistent with record, Supplemental Rule 6001.330 prescribes these methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifeline program — annual disclosure statements and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and lower tier participants in the Lifeline program must file annual disclosure statements, upon penalty of perjury, reporting all required disclosures or certifying they have no reportable disclosures; primary tier participants may file on behalf of lower tier participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WCB to develop an information collection for these annual certifications. Primary tier participants must maintain documentation substantiating required certifications for at least the three full preceding calendar years and provide such documentation to the Commission or USAC upon request. Non-filing may be considered 'credible information' for imposing funding holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: USF competitive bidding short-form disclosure rule
rubrics_metrics.description: At the competitive bidding short-form stage, the Commission's review is limited to whether the applicant is presently excluded or disqualified; a winning bidder must make additional required disclosures in the long-form application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrow option preserves auction speed and places risk on the applicant for inaccurate short-form certifications; long-form disclosures can lead to enforcement if initial certifications were incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRS and NDBEDP program-specific disclosure timing
rubrics_metrics.description: TRS providers and NDBEDP providers and their lower tier participants must file required disclosures as part of certification and renewal applications. Internet-based TRS providers must update disclosures within 60 days of any change. Each certified NDBEDP provider shall file updates every six months and file notifications of substantive change if disclosure bears on certification qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 64 of the rules is amended to implement these program-specific disclosure and update timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency flexibility and remedies for unfavorable disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission retains flexibility to pursue tailored measures in response to unfavorable disclosures, including but not limited to suspension/debarment, precluding participation in a transaction, approving only after an administrative agreement/compliance plan, denying an application, terminating participation, or referring matters to the SDO for limited denial or exclusion proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant bureaus/offices (e.g., CGB, WCB) are authorized to determine remedies in the first instance and program administrators must develop policies/procedures for reviewing unfavorable disclosures. Supplemental Rule 6001.345 and section 180.340 support addressing risks without resorting automatically to exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to err on side of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are urged to err on the side of disclosure in close cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhanced disclosures facilitate program integrity and administrative efficiency and the benefits of combating waste, fraud, and abuse outweigh incidental burdens of modified disclosure requirements.
